findings.summary: Redirects were built from the client-controlled Host header, making this unauthenticated route an open redirect (CWE-644). Fixed: origin now comes from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL; Host and x-forwarded-host are no longer read. Verified by probe and 7 regression tests.
next-parameter validation used a startsWith check that missed backslash variants like /\evil.com. Fixed: the candidate is parsed against our origin and URL.origin compared.
exchangeCodeForSession had no try/catch, so a GoTrue transport failure surfaced as a 500 instead of the specified error screen. Fixed.
An English aria-label sat over Vietnamese visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name), added to satisfy a test regex. Fixed: override removed and the test now matches the localized name.
C8 originally passed vacuously against a 404 and never exercised the guarded redirect it exists to protect. Fixed: it now forces a token refresh with an expired access token.
The suite raced next dev's on-demand client-bundle compilation, failing C3/C5 deterministically on a cold start. Fixed with a browser warmup in the setup project.
Keyboard focus is not returned to the trigger after choosing an option. Real but minor; left for the user to decide rather than changed after inspection.
Route-guard prefix matching is slightly broader than intended (e.g. /todo-archive would match /todo). No such route exists today.
Self-referential CSS custom properties work only because of cascade scoping; fragile if reused elsewhere.

RISK-01: hero artwork absent because MoMorph's render endpoint was down all session. Ships the recorded geometry over a #00101A fallback; the real file drops in with zero code change. Accepted by the user as ORCH-05.

Open dropdown rendered VN/EN as bare text while the trigger showed a flag, because OPTIONS carried no icon reference. Fixed: each option owns its flag. RED proved first by stashing the fix (C3b failed toHaveCount(1)->0). The design defines no open-state variant, so the closed state's flag+label rule was used as the contract.

The hydration warmup located its target by an accessible-name regex that also matched the Next dev-tools button; the resulting strict-mode violation was swallowed by a catch that then let the caller print 'hydration complete'. The warmup was only working as a side effect of goto(). Fixed: unambiguous aria-haspopup locator, an actual listbox-open check as hydration proof, and the catch now rethrows rather than reporting a false success.
